1_auditor_liveness_cannot_depend_on_a_tr.why_it_is_severe: An audit hook whose liveness depends on an unrelated training feature is inert by construction, and reports zero rather than erroring -- indistinguishable from 'nothing went wrong'.

3_overlay_must_be_verified_by_PROVENANCE.found: OP7's BASE behaviour-tree profile already carries min_alive_for_defender=2 -- the exact value the Pole-A overlay sets.
3_overlay_must_be_verified_by_PROVENANCE.why_it_is_severe: The field the overlay SETS is already present in the other pole's base profile, so the observable effect carries no information about installation. Only genome_id and requested_overlay record what was installed.
3_overlay_must_be_verified_by_PROVENANCE.fix: presence is read from genome_id and requested_overlay, which are provenance fields recording what was INSTALLED, not what the resolved profile happens to contain
3_overlay_must_be_verified_by_PROVENANCE.regression_test: a check that passes when genome_id is None but the resolved value coincidentally matches must be treated as broken
3_overlay_must_be_verified_by_PROVENANCE.CORRECTION: An earlier draft of this record claimed an effect-based check would produce a confident false PASS. That overstated it and a mutation check disproved it. Measured from the real captured evidence: OP6-with-overlay and OP7-base BOTH read min_alive_for_defender = 2. So an effect-based check cannot separate the poles in EITHER direction. On the correct configuration it flags all 16 OP7 envs -- a false FAIL that would send someone debugging a non-existent problem. A one-sided variant asserting only 'OP6 has the value' would pass with no overlay installed anywhere -- a false PASS. Which error you get depends on how the check is written; that it is wrong does not.
